paragraphs.text: This page puts the same social move in three sizes. In situation A two people who do not know each other yet stop, greet, ask how the other is and exchange names — that is the longest thing you will have to manage today. Situation B is the version you will use fifty times a week: a quick hello to someone you already know, one line each, and you both walk on. Situation C is only about leaving.

Read them with the sound on if you can, then read them again without. Notice how short the turns are — nobody builds a long sentence to say {{de:Hallo}} or {{de:Tschüs!}}. The full sentences show up in exactly two places: asking how someone is, and asking what they are called, {{de:Entschuldigung, wie heißt du?}}
Wer bist du? — Ich heiße Niklas. · Wie geht's dir? — Danke, gut. Und dir? — Auch gut, danke. · Tschüs Julia! Bis bald!

Learn the reply as tightly as the question. Every question on this page arrives with its answer already attached, and having the answer ready is what keeps a first conversation from stalling after hello.

blocks.headline: Situation A — Hallo, ich bin Julia

paragraphs.text: Julia and Niklas meet outside, exchange greetings, ask about each other and give their names. Listen for the moment where Julia says who she is before she asks.

turns.speaker: Julia
turns.german: Hallo, ich bin Julia. Und du? Wer bist du?
turns.english: Hello, I'm Julia. And you? Who are you?

blocks.headline: Situationen B und C — Wie geht's? Tschüs!

paragraphs.text: The second meeting is between people who already know each other, so the question drops the word after it — {{de:Wie geht's?}} with no {{de:dir}}. The third scene is the shortest of the page: three words, and everybody leaves.
